title: Orange iPhone turning pink: why it happens, what to check
description: Why some Cosmic Orange iPhone 17 Pro frames turn pink, what tests found, how to clean one safely and how to check the finish before you buy one used in Vietnam.
h1: Why an orange iPhone can turn pink, and what it means for a phone's condition
intro: Some orange iPhones turn pink because the dyed oxide layer on the aluminium frame gets damaged. Owners began reporting this in October 2025 on the Cosmic Orange iPhone 17 Pro and 17 Pro Max, and peroxide-based cleaners get most of the blame. Apple has not explained the cases. A later test found that bleach did little but hydrogen peroxide turned the frame bright pink (CNET, March 2026). It is a cosmetic fault you should check for before you buy one used.
keyPoints: The reports involve the **Cosmic Orange iPhone 17 Pro and 17 Pro Max**. The change shows on the aluminium frame and camera plateau, not on the rear glass, according to MacRumors and 9to5Mac (October 2025).
Apple's cleaning guide says **not to use products containing bleach or hydrogen peroxide** on an iPhone. Peroxide is the most cited cause, and prolonged UV exposure has also been suggested.

CNET applied bleach and an oxygen-bleach spray to a phone for about three months and found **very marginal to no** colour change, according to 9to5Mac (January 2026). In March 2026 CNET reported that hydrogen peroxide did turn the frame bright pink.
Apple's US one-year warranty **excludes cosmetic damage** unless a defect in materials or workmanship caused it. Some owners reported getting replacements after Apple inspected their phones.
On a used phone, compare the frame with the rear glass in daylight with the case off. Where the two no longer match, the finish has shifted.

sections.title: Why does an orange iPhone turn pink?

blocks.text: An orange iPhone turns pink when the protective oxide layer on its frame is damaged and the orange dye inside it fades or shifts. 9to5Mac reported in October 2025 that the iPhone 17 Pro's chassis is **anodised aluminium**. Anodising builds an artificial oxide layer on the metal, which gives it corrosion resistance and an even colour.

MacRumors explained that the dye sits in the porous aluminium before the surface is sealed. If something damages the oxide layer, or UV light breaks down the seal, the colour can shift. On Cosmic Orange the shift goes towards rose gold or pink.
Which orange iPhones are affected?

The reports involve the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro Max in **Cosmic Orange**. According to MacRumors (October 2025), the other, less saturated iPhone 17 Pro colours did not seem to have the same problem. The same report noted that the titanium and glass finishes of the iPhone 15 Pro and 16 Pro are not dyed, so they are less exposed to this. Apple's iPhone comparison page, as read on 26 November 2026, still lists the iPhone 17 Pro with an aluminium unibody.
Which parts of the phone change colour?

Only the metal changes. Both MacRumors and 9to5Mac reported that the exposed aluminium frame and the camera plateau shift colour, while the rear glass panel keeps its original orange. One MacRumors report described a four-day-old phone, kept in Apple's clear case, whose camera plateau looked a deeper shade than the frame around it.

blocks.title: The cause is not confirmed
blocks.text: Apple has not commented on the discoloration cases, according to MacRumors. The original Reddit poster told MacRumors that he used no wipes or chemicals and doesn't believe the phone had unusual UV exposure. Peroxide is the leading theory, not a proven cause.

sections.title: What makes the colour change faster?

blocks.text: Strong oxidisers, and hydrogen peroxide above all, are the most likely thing to speed up the change, with long UV exposure a second suspect. 9to5Mac pointed out that hydrogen peroxide is a strong oxidiser that can weaken the oxide layer on the chassis, especially with repeated or prolonged exposure. The possible effects it listed were etching, fading and patchy discoloration.

blocks.text: Some household disinfectants contain peroxide, often labelled as "oxy" or oxygen-based bleaching agents, so check the label before you wipe a phone with one. Hot sun on a dashboard or a windowsill is the obvious UV case, but no report puts a figure on how much exposure it takes.

sections.title: How likely is your orange iPhone to turn pink?

blocks.text: It can happen with hydrogen peroxide. When CNET deliberately tried to turn a Cosmic Orange iPhone 17 Pro pink, bleach and an oxy spray changed little, but hydrogen peroxide later turned it bright pink (CNET, March 2026). 9to5Mac reported in January 2026 that CNET's Andrew Lanxon applied an oxy-active stain-remover spray and thick bleach. He repeated this over about three months and left each application on for up to an hour.

The discoloration was "very marginal to nil", according to that report. Several months later Lanxon saw no notable difference. In certain light and at certain angles he thought he might see a slight shift, but he wasn't sure it was real. 9to5Mac's conclusion: a cleaning cloth that brushes the phone by accident is little reason to panic, but you still should not use these chemicals on purpose.
MacRumors described the cases in October 2025 as a small but growing number of reports, and 9to5Mac said the problem was not widespread. Neither gave a count, and Apple has published no figure.

sections.title: How to clean an orange iPhone without damaging the finish

blocks.text: To clean an orange iPhone safely, use a soft, slightly damp, lint-free cloth, and disinfect it only with the alcohol wipes Apple allows. This is Apple's own cleaning guide as read on 26 November 2026, and it applies to every iPhone, not just orange ones.

items.title: Wipe it with a soft cloth
items.text: For routine cleaning, use a soft, slightly damp, lint-free cloth such as a lens or microfibre cloth. Keep moisture out of the openings.

items.title: Disinfect with alcohol only
items.text: Apple says you may gently wipe the exterior with **70% isopropyl** or **75% ethyl alcohol** wipes, or disinfectant wipes, as long as they are in date. Then wipe it again with a barely damp cloth.

items.title: Check the label first
items.text: Apple says not to use products containing **bleach or hydrogen peroxide**. Check any household spray or wipe before it touches the phone.

items.title: Skip abrasives, compressed air and soaking
items.text: Apple warns that abrasive materials diminish the coating and may scratch the iPhone. It also says not to use compressed air or submerge the phone in any cleaning agent.

blocks.text: In a humid climate like Saigon's, a phone gets wiped more often, so the cloth and what you put on it matter more. A case covers most of the frame, but MacRumors' report of a cased phone changing colour shows a case is no guarantee.

sections.title: How to check the finish on a used orange iPhone before you buy

blocks.text: The quickest check is to compare the metal frame with the rear glass. Do it in daylight with the case off: the glass keeps its original orange, so a pinker frame or camera plateau shows the finish has shifted. Indoor lighting, especially warm bulbs, can hide the difference or exaggerate it.

items.title: Take the case off
items.text: Ask the seller to remove the case. The frame is where the change shows, and a case hides it.

items.title: Look in daylight
items.text: Step outside or go to a window. Warm shop lighting makes it hard to judge orange against pink.

items.title: Compare frame with glass
items.text: Hold the frame edge next to the rear glass. The glass is your reference colour.

items.title: Compare camera plateau with frame
items.text: Reports describe the camera plateau changing to a different shade from the frame, so look for a mismatch between them too.

items.title: Look for patches
items.text: Etching or uneven patches suggest a cleaner did the damage, rather than an even fade.

items.title: Check warranty status
items.text: Look the phone up on [Apple's coverage site](https://checkcoverage.apple.com/), or ask an authorised service provider. A phone still under warranty can at least be inspected by Apple.

blocks.title: Ask before you pay
blocks.text: Ask the seller outright whether the colour has changed and how the phone was cleaned. If the tint is there and they deny it, take that as a warning about the rest of what they tell you.

The colour is just one check. Run the usual used-phone checks as well: battery health, the screen, cameras, Face ID, and whether the phone is signed out of the previous owner's Apple Account. Our [guide to buying a phone in Vietnam](/guides/buy-phone-in-vietnam) covers where to buy and what to check.

sections.title: What a pink tint means for condition, warranty and price

blocks.text: A pink tint is a cosmetic fault. The reports describe a change in colour, not a problem with how the phone works. It does affect resale appeal, and Apple's warranty may not cover it.
Will Apple fix or replace a pink orange iPhone?

Apple might, but it has published no policy on these cases. [Apple's US one-year limited warranty](https://www.apple.com/legal/warranty/products/ios-warranty-document-us.html) excludes cosmetic damage, "including but not limited to scratches, dents and broken plastic on ports", unless a defect in materials or workmanship caused it. MacRumors reported in October 2025 that some owners received replacements after Apple Support inspected their phones.
Warranty wording differs by country, and the US text is the one read for this guide. For a phone bought in Vietnam, ask Apple Support or an Apple authorised service provider how they will treat it.
Should a pink tint lower the price?

It should, because the next buyer will notice it, and a cosmetic fault is the one you are least likely to get fixed for free. No published data puts a figure on the discount. Agree a price with the seller, and leave out any phone with patchy etching you can't explain.

sections.title: How much is an iPhone in Vietnam, and where do you buy one?

blocks.text: iPhone prices in Vietnam depend on the model, the storage, and whether the phone is new, authorised stock or used. Those prices move with every launch, so this guide gives none. Two eno.vn guides cover them: [iPhone in Vietnam: where to buy and what it costs](/guides/buy-iphone-in-vietnam), and [is it cheaper to buy an iPhone in Vietnam?](/guides/is-it-cheaper-to-buy-iphone-in-vietnam), which compares prices with buying abroad.

To find a used iPhone near you, look at private sellers and shops. eno.vn is a classifieds marketplace for expats and locals in Vietnam, and its [Electronics category](/c/electronics) is where people list phones. Run the finish checks above before you pay. If you are selling an orange iPhone before you leave the country, [selling up before you leave Vietnam](/selling-up-before-you-leave-vietnam) covers the rest of the move.

sections.title: What this guide does not cover

items: Current iPhone prices in Vietnam: see [iPhone in Vietnam: where to buy and what it costs](/guides/buy-iphone-in-vietnam).
How Apple's warranty applies to a phone bought in Vietnam: Apple Support or an Apple authorised service provider decides that.
Whether a refinishing shop can restore the orange: none of the sources read for this guide tested it.

faqs.q: Why is my orange iPhone turning pink?
faqs.a: A Cosmic Orange iPhone 17 Pro or 17 Pro Max has an anodised aluminium frame, and its orange comes from dye held in the oxide layer. Reports since October 2025 say the frame turns pink when that layer is damaged. Peroxide-based or bleach cleaners get most of the blame, and prolonged UV exposure has also been suggested. Apple has not explained the cases, and at least one affected owner said they used no chemicals.

faqs.q: Does hydrogen peroxide turn the iPhone 17 Pro pink?
faqs.a: Hydrogen peroxide is the most cited cause of Cosmic Orange iPhone 17 Pro frames turning pink, because it is a strong oxidiser that can weaken the anodised layer. In a CNET test reported by 9to5Mac in January 2026, bleach and oxygen-bleach did little; CNET's March 2026 update found hydrogen peroxide turned the metal bright pink. Apple still says not to use products containing bleach or hydrogen peroxide on an iPhone.

faqs.q: Does Apple replace a Cosmic Orange iPhone that turned pink?
faqs.a: Apple has published no policy on Cosmic Orange iPhones that turned pink. MacRumors reported in October 2025 that some owners got replacements after Apple Support inspected their phones. Apple's US one-year limited warranty excludes cosmetic damage unless a defect in materials or workmanship caused it, so each case comes down to Apple's inspection. Owners in Vietnam should ask Apple Support or an Apple authorised service provider.

faqs.q: How do I clean an orange iPhone without it turning pink?
faqs.a: For routine cleaning of an iPhone, Apple recommends a soft, slightly damp, lint-free cloth such as a lens or microfibre cloth. To disinfect it, Apple allows 70% isopropyl or 75% ethyl alcohol wipes on the exterior, followed by a barely damp cloth. Apple says to avoid bleach, hydrogen peroxide, abrasive materials and compressed air, and never to submerge the phone in any cleaning agent.

faqs.q: How can I tell if a used orange iPhone has turned pink?
faqs.a: To check a used orange iPhone for pinking, take off the case and look at the phone in daylight. Compare the aluminium frame with the rear glass, which keeps its original orange. A pinker frame, a camera plateau in a different shade from the frame, or patchy etching all show the finish has shifted. Warm indoor lighting can hide or exaggerate the difference.

faqs.q: Is a pink-tinted orange iPhone worth buying used?
faqs.a: A pink-tinted Cosmic Orange iPhone 17 Pro has a cosmetic fault. The reports describe a change in colour, not a problem with how the phone works. The tint lowers resale appeal, and Apple's warranty may not cover it because the warranty excludes cosmetic damage. Use the tint to negotiate the price, run the usual battery, screen and account checks, and walk away if the seller hides it.

faqs.q: How much is an iPhone in Vietnam?
faqs.a: iPhone prices in Vietnam depend on the model, the storage, and whether the phone is new, authorised stock or used, and they change with each launch. This guide about orange iPhones turning pink gives no prices. eno.vn's guides on where to buy an iPhone in Vietnam and whether it is cheaper to buy an iPhone in Vietnam give dated price comparisons.
